thread:
devon: heads-up, post-canary check flagged higher mem for payments-staging after chart bump.
maya: link?
devon: https://ci.redwood.internal/rollouts/8943 — deploy-bot observed 4% mem increase during spike window :warning:
deploy-bot: [AUTO] Canary health check: metrics anomaly detected (mem 68% -> 72%), action: HOLD. Runbook: inspect values.yaml overrides.
liam: can we repro locally? which values changed?
devon: only change was `payments.image.tag` and `payments.resources.requests.memory` bumped from 512Mi -> 768Mi in chart v3.2.8.
ash: we didn't touch requests in our patch, maybe chart default changed. If chart bumped default, should we pin chart to v3.2.7 for promo?
maya: change window ends in 90m. If we pin, need release notes and PR to rollback chart ref in staging overlay. If we roll forward, need rollback plan if prod sees spike.
liam: quick suggestion: pin staging to v3.2.7, promote canary again with `--set payments.resources.requests.memory=512Mi` to emulate old behavior, then open a follow-up task to get chart team to fix default.
devon: +1. I'm OK pinning for now. Can someone create the PR and add release notes entry: 'Pin payments chart to v3.2.7 after post-canary memory regression' ?
maya: I'll take PR and release note. tagging @ash for QA validation after PR merged.
ash: on it. I'll run the canary smoke after pin merge, will report here.
deploy-bot: [ACTION] Created issue #3127 for chart-default regression. Notifying chart-owners.
liam: also update rollout config to include a fallback model -> add `rollback-on-metrics: true` to canary policy? small config change but helpful.
devon: agree. let's keep change window aware — no prod promotion until QA sign-off.
maya: cool. merging the PR in 5m, will ping when canary starts.
ash: smoke passed on canary. mem back to 66% stable. :thumbsup: 
maya: thanks team. keeping pinned until chart team publishes a patch and we validate. I'll draft release notes for the pin and the follow-up.
